fact: 2009-12-10：Clare 坐在芝加哥艺术博物馆的 Ando Gallery——博物馆亚洲部里的暗室，十六根木柱、六只十三世纪陶罐、四扇柔光日本屏风、一条长凳；她已坐了两小时，Alba 在 Kimy 那里，她今天没有别处要去。
quote: Thursday, December 10, 2009 (Clare is 38, Beck is 33) … Clare: I am sitting in the Ando Gallery in the Art Institute of Chicago. It is a secret space inside the museum’s austere Asian Department, a dark room filled with sixteen wooden columns, six thirteenth-century pots, four softly illuminated Japanese screens and a bench.

fact: Henry 死了快三年，她仍放不下：总觉得还在听、在等；他的骨灰装在一只极简日本骨灰瓮里，放在她画室入口旁的小红桌上——进门后它就在身后，这是 Henry 在她心里位置的隐喻：第一件想起的事，然后必须往前走。
quote: Henry died almost three years ago, and I can’t seem to let him go. I am always listening, waiting, expecting. … Henry’s ashes are in a minimalist Japanese urn which sits on a small red table near the entrance to my studio.

fact: 一个穿长大衣、厚底鞋的女人进来，深色头发像一圈烟雾竖起，小圆眼镜在暗光里反金；她在屏风旁站了一下，转身要坐长凳，看见 Clare 时迟疑；Clare 朝凳尾示意请坐；两人并肩坐了一阵，女人坐了将近一小时，离开时四目相对、微笑。
quote: A woman enters the gallery. She is wearing a long coat and chunky shoes; her steps make loud thunks against the wooden floor. … She hesitates when she sees me. I gesture toward the end of the bench, Please, go ahead, sit down. She nods and sits.

fact: 一周后（12-17）女人又来，直接走到长凳坐下说 Hello；她手叠在膝上，把帽子放在两人之间，身上有雪、洗发水、湿羊毛的气味；Clare 挪不开注意力，偷看她、想记住她的脸；她走后 Clare 拿出速写本画她（深眼睛、浓眉、微翘小鼻、宽嘴、黑人、高梳的发、大圈耳环），画得不对；此后她天天去 Ando Gallery 去了两周，女人再没来。
quote: Thursday, December 17, 2009 … I remember this woman: she walks directly to the bench and sits down. She turns to me and says, “Hello.” … I go to the Ando Gallery every day for two weeks, but she doesn’t come back.

fact: 2010-03-18，Clare 在博物馆 coat check 附近解大衣扣时撞见她：这回看清了灰发、比记忆里高、眉上穿了环；Clare 脱口说「Oh, there you are」，立刻后悔；女人没认出她，疑惑地答「Here I am」，去排队存衣；Clare 没进馆就回家，在高架车上想：自从 Henry 死后一切都像随机的。
quote: Thursday, March 18, 2010 … “Oh, there you are,” I say and instantly regret it. She doesn’t recognize me and gives me a doubtful look. “Here I am,” she agrees and moves along to stand in the coat check line.

fact: 2010-03-23，Clare 穿过现代艺术展厅去和 Charisse 午饭，Charisse 在 Mary Reynolds 展厅（杜尚《La Boîte-en-valise》玻璃柜前）把她介绍给「Rebecka Charles」——正是画廊里的女人；对方笑着说「Oh, there you are」，Clare 答「Here I am」，握手时「觉得一个未来落到了位置上」。
quote: “Clare, hello. I hope you don’t mind, I brought someone to meet you. Rebecka Charles, meet Clare DeTamble.” … “Oh, there you are,” she says, and she holds out her hand. “Here I am,” I reply. I take her hand and feel a future fall into place.

fact: 午餐上 Beck 讲她的虚拟博物馆：渡渡鸟、1990 年加德纳博物馆被盗的画、底特律已成空地的房子、巴米扬大佛、一堆配不成对的袜子、一屋子旧情书，还有她来芝加哥前死掉的猫 Ida B 在里面走动；她管它叫「Museum of Lost Souls」，说里面没有人，但可以有。
quote: “Mostly art, but other things, too. … I’ve got that dodo from the Museum of Natural History in New York, all those paintings that were stolen from the Gardner Museum in 1990, a lot of houses that used to be in Detroit but now they are just empty lots, the Buddhas of Bamiyan, a pile of unmatched socks, a room full of old love letters.” … “I’ve been calling it the Museum of Lost Souls.”

fact: Beck 说自己的丈夫「丢了」：可能精神分裂，诊断没定，状况很糟、出过事，她没法照顾他，「不安全」；她从底特律搬来 SAIC 教书是想重新开始，但被问「成了吗」答「还没有」。Clare 说不想重新开始、想继续，但自己「像在模仿自己的作品」，并承认自己在「等」——像对孩子说的：走丢了就待在原地别乱走，她把一切保持成 Henry 死时的样子，以防他回来。
quote: “I lost my husband a few years ago. I mean, I didn’t lose him; he died.” … “I sort of know how that is. My husband is lost.” … “I don’t think I want to begin again,” I say. “I want to continue.” … “I’m just imitating my own work.”

fact: 散场后 Charisse 说 Beck 正在打一场难看的离婚、住在 South Loop 的极简工作室（大部分东西还在底特律），通常很内向；她当场把 Beck 的号码发给 Clare，说「Henry 不在了，你现在得有意愿地往前走……她是孤独的，你也是孤独的，两个孤独相遇、喝咖啡」（近里尔克语）；次日早晨 Clare 发短信「Hey, it’s Clare. How are you?」，三分钟后收到「Not too bad. I have an almond croissant and an espresso…」，世界忽然变好。
quote: “I know you’re used to things snapping into place without you having to lift a finger. But Henry is gone, you have to proceed with intention now. Make stuff happen, Clare. She’s lonely. You’re lonely. Two solitudes that greet each other, and have coffee, and all that.” … Three minutes later a reply appears: Not too bad. I have an almond croissant and an espresso and it’s a pretty day.
